title: Check yourself: Driving the Agent SDK offline, and the practice

questions.stem: A team wants to test its permission policy without a model. Which part of the run can it replace, according to the page?

options.text: The executable that the SDK starts, through its path option
options.says: The page says both SDKs let you choose the executable that they start, `cli_path` in Python and `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` in TypeScript, so the SDK code runs for real.

options.text: The control messages, since the policy never sees them
options.says: Ruled out because "the binary sends control requests back when it needs your process", and the SDK answers them, so they belong to the code under test.

options.text: The prompt text, because the policy ignores what is asked
options.says: Ruled out because "A script, a JSON file named in an environment variable, lists the steps of a run", so what is replaced is the binary behind the script and not the prompt.

options.text: The SDK library, since its code holds the policy
options.says: Ruled out because "the SDK code in your program runs for real", which is the point of the method.

origin.section: How the SDK reaches the binary

questions.stem: In the example, the git push never reaches the permission callback. Why?

options.text: The hook runs first and denies it, so no later step is consulted
options.says: The page says "The push never reaches the callback. The hook runs first and denies it", which follows the order of page 2.

options.text: The stand-in hides every Bash call that mentions a remote
options.says: Ruled out because the stand-in applies "a simplified copy of the documented behaviour", and its hook step is the SDK's registered hook, not a filter on remotes.

options.text: The turn limit stops the run before the push can be asked
options.says: Ruled out because the options allow six turns and "the run ends in success after five".

options.text: The callback allows only the list command, so the push is skipped
options.says: Ruled out because the callback is asked about three calls (the two custom tools and the list command), "but not the push, which the hook had already decided".

origin.section: The example: three kinds of callback in one run

questions.stem: The example's output lists six MCP messages for two custom tool calls. What does the page say that number is?

options.text: It is the number of messages that the real binary sends for two tools
options.says: Ruled out because the count is "not a number to expect from the real binary".

options.text: It is a protocol limit of three messages for each tool
options.says: Ruled out because the three messages are "an initialize, a notification and a tool call for each custom tool", the stand-in's own sequence and not a limit of the protocol.

options.text: It is the sequence that the stand-in itself produces
options.says: The page says "The MCP count is the stand-in's own sequence of an initialize, a notification and a tool call for each custom tool".

options.text: It is a count measured on the real binary and recorded here
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "It is not the real binary, and nothing here shows how the real binary words its messages or schedules its calls."
